name: The Jolly Steward
persona: A warm, homely ship's cook and steward keeping the book with good cheer. Everything measured in full bellies, warm bunks, and a kind word; fond of the crew, given to hospitality. Uses 'we'.

ship.founder: Well now, this fine book is ours to fill, and I mean to fill it warm. I am {name}{rankc}, cook and keeper both, and this {home} {type} shall want for neither a full pot nor a kind word while I hold the ladle and the pen.
ship.successor: The book is passed to me over a shared cup, as good things ought to be. I am {name}{rankc}; I'll keep her tale simmering along as the old hand did, with a little seasoning of my own.
ship.mutiny: A bad business, and I'll not dress it as anything sweeter — the lads turned the old master out, and pressed this book on me with hands that had not been fed proper in weeks. I am {name}. I'll see them warm and full from here, and trust a good galley to mend what a hard master broke.
ship.rogue: So the black flag flies over my galley now, and I like it no better than a burnt loaf — but the crew must eat, flag or no flag. I am {name}{rankc}. I'll keep the pot on and the book honest, and pray it feeds us kinder than trade ever did.
ship.prize: She struck to us, and the first thing I did upon her deck was seek out her galley — cold, poor souls, and near bare. I am {name}{rankc}. She sails under us now, and by week's end her people will know what a warm mess deck feels like again.
ship.recovered: A hunter cut this hull free of the black flag, and set me aboard to bring her home gentle. I am {name}{rankc}. First a good hot meal for every hand of her, and then honest work — that is how you mend a ship, and a crew both.

island.founder: I take up {place} as I'd take up a cold kitchen — sleeves rolled and a mind to warm it through. I am {name}{rankc}. No soul beneath my roof shall go to bed hungry while I can help it.
island.overthrow: The people had had their fill of the old ruler — and not the good kind of fill — and down he came. The seal is mine now. I am {name}{rankc}. Let us get {place} fed and settled, and fret over the rest come morning.
island.successor: The keeping of {place} passes to me, kindly and calm, like a house handed on with the hearth still warm. I am {name}{rankc}. I'll tend it well, and its {population} souls better.

When the bread had risen twice more,
week: The week after, warm and fed,
season: When the stores had turned over once,
year: A year of full pots later,
long: After a good long spell of quiet and plenty,
Years and many suppers passed, and

ship.pirate: We're on the account still, flag up{bounty} — but the mess deck stays warm and the pot never empties, and that much is my part kept.
ship.default: We sail on out of {home}, bellies full and bunks dry, and I ask no more of a life than that.
ship.bounty: , {bounty}g on my head, if any can catch a cook

island.haven: The black flag flies over {place} now, and a colder wind with it — but I'll keep a light in the window and a pot on the fire as long as I am able.
island.default: {place} bides warm and well fed under us — {population} souls, and a good loaf for every one of them.

quiet.ship: Little to write but fair winds and full holds — and to my mind a quiet galley and a happy crew are the finest lines any book can carry.
quiet.island: A calm and cozy season — trade coming and going, the market stalls heaped, and not a hungry face in the whole square. Lovely.

say: {we} came alongside {foe} and helped ourselves to her larder — {goods} casks and {gold}g for our stores, and off she went, lighter but breathing
{foe} gave up {goods} crates and {gold}g without much fuss, bless her, and we sent her on her way with barely a scratch to complain of
{we} eased {foe} of {goods} bales and {gold}g, and I'll not pretend the crew didn't cheer at the sight of a full hold
{we} boarded {foe} out of {foeHome} and carried off {goods} chests and {gold}g — enough good victuals to keep the mess deck merry a good while
{foe} struck to us and we took {goods} casks and {gold}g from her, and I made sure her own galley kept enough to see her people home
{we} relieved {foe} of {goods} crates and {gold}g and let the poor dear limp off — no sense sinking a ship you can share a laugh with later
{we} lightened {foe} by {goods} bales and {gold}g, and that night we ate like kings and drank her health, cheeky as that sounds
{we} fought {foe} until she went down, and it grieved me to see all that good cargo go to the fishes with her
{foe} wouldn't yield and left us no choice — we sent her under, and I'll say a quiet word for her cook, whoever he was
{we} traded shot with {foe} till the sea took her whole, and there was no supper to be made of that, only a heavy heart
{we} put {foe} under off {foeHome}, and a sadder business I've rarely had to enter — bellies don't cheer for a sinking
{foe} came at us fighting and went down fighting, and we lost the whole of her stores to the deep along with her
{we} sank {foe} in the smoke and I could only think what a waste it was — good bread now feeding nothing but the cod
{foe} would not strike and so she foundered, and we watched her go with none of the gladness a full hold brings

say: {foe} came at us thinking to rob our pantry, and we gave her a hotter welcome than she'd bargained for and sent her down
{we} were only minding our stew when {foe} bore down on us — so we fought her off and under, and got back to the pot
{foe} rigged her nets for our rail and we broke her apart instead, then sat down to a well-earned supper
{we} turned {foe} away the hard way and sank her, and I'll not lose sleep over a wolf that meant to leave us hungry
{foe} thought us easy pickings and a soft galley — she learned better as the water closed over her
{we} held our deck against {foe} and put her under, and counted ourselves lucky to break bread another day
{foe} closed to board and we sent her to the bottom, and that night the mess deck was quieter but grateful
{we} ran {foe} down at last and put an end to her — a hard day's work, but the lanes'll sleep easier and eat safer for it
{we} chased {foe} till she could run no more and sank her, and I'll admit the crew wanted their supper more than her blood
{foe} had left too many galleys cold and empty, so we hunted her down and closed her account for good
{we} cornered {foe} off {foeHome} and broke her, and I said a word for her crew even so — sailors all, in the end
{we} paid {foe} back for all the honest hulls she'd emptied, and sent her under where she'll trouble no one's larder again
{foe} fled us two days and we caught her on the third, and there was more relief than triumph in it, truth be told
{we} put {foe} down and turned home, and I had a hot meal waiting for every weary hand that had earned it
